title: Our Town Hides When The WHISTLE Blows 📯
premise: When the town whistle blows, at any hour, everyone goes down to their basement until it stops. I'm 24, back living with Dad, and our basement has gained one step every whistle, from thirteen to twenty-six. My grandpa next door, in the only house with no basement, makes tea.
twist: Nothing walks the streets: the thing lives under the town and blows the whistle itself to call everyone down, and every time they come it pulls their stairs one step closer. Grandpa built on stone blocks so it could never call him. I blow the whistle from the top and its own rule sends it deeper down.
world: a bright summer street of pastel clapboard houses with a green iron pole and a brass whistle in the middle of the road, cellar steps going down, a face as wide as a basement far under the street
